docs.title: pkgKitten: Create packages that purr
docs.text:
The base R function package.skeleton() is very useful for creating new packages for R. It is also very upsetting as it has been producing the same files which trigger R CMD check in the exact same way.

And as something terrible happens each time R CMD check barks, this package offers a wrapper function kitten() which leaves an adorable little package behind which does not upset R CMD check.

So just think of the kittens.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
The package is on CRAN and can be installed via a standard

install.packages("pkgKitten")

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: Package documentation, help pages, and more is also available here.

docs.title: Create a very simple package
docs.text: Source code

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The kitten function creates an (almost) empty example package.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
kitten(name = "anRpackage", path = ".", author, maintainer, email,
  githubuser = NA_character_, license = "GPL (>= 2)", puppy = TRUE,
  bunny = TRUE)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: name The name of the package to be created, defaults to “anRpackage” path The path to the location where the package is to be created, defaults to the current directory. author The name of the author, defaults to the result of fullname (or “Your Name” as fallback). maintainer The name of the maintainer, also defaults to fullname or author if the latter is given. email The maintainer email address, defaults to email_address (or “your@email.com” as fallback). githubuser The maintainer github user, defaults to NA_character\_ implying “URL” and “BugReports” fields are not being set. One can call gh_username outside of continuous integration settings. license The license of the new package, defaults to “GPL-2”. puppy Toggle whether tinytest::puppy add unit testing, default to true (but conditional on tinytest being installed). bunny Toggle whether roxygen2 should be used for the the creation of Rd files from R, default is true (but also conditional on roxygen2 being install).

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
The kitten function can be used to initialize a simple package. It is created with the minimal number of files. What distinguished it from the function package.skeleton() in base R (which it actually calls) is that the resulting package passes R CMD check cleanly.

Because every time you create a new package which does not pass R CMD check, a kitten experiences an existential trauma. Just think about the kittens.

docs.title: Value
docs.text: Nothing is returned as the function is invoked for its side effect of creating a new package.

docs.title: Author(s)
docs.text: Dirk Eddelbuettel

docs.title: Create simple packages using the kitten function.
Description
docs.text:
The base R function package.skeleton() is very helpful, but insist on creating packages which do not pass R CMD check.

That is silly,

This package helps with this issue. No more, no less.

docs.title: Author(s)
docs.text: Dirk Eddelbuettel wrote the package and maintains it.

docs.title: See Also
docs.text: package.skeleton, the ‘Writing R Extensions’ manual.

docs.title: Create a very simple package help page
docs.text: Source code

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The playWithPerPackageHelpPage function creates an basic package help page.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
playWithPerPackageHelpPage(name = "anRpackage", path = ".",
  maintainer = "Your Name", email = "your@mail.com")

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: name The name of the package to be created, defaults to “anRpackage” path The path to the location where the package is to be created, defaults to the current directory. maintainer The name of the maintainer, defaults to “Your Name” or author if the latter is given. email The maintainer email address.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
The playWithPerPackageHelpPage function can be used to create a simple help page for a package.

It has been split off from the kitten function so that it can be called from other packages. As such, it is also exported from pkgKitten.

docs.title: Value
docs.text: Nothing is returned as the function is invoked for its side effect of creating a new package.

docs.title: Author(s)
docs.text: Dirk Eddelbuettel
